example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, every journal entry, 1 July to 30 September 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

messages.text: Can you review our journal entries for the third quarter before the audit committee meets?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need nine answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
What are your approval limits? I never assume one.
What size of amount is material for you?
Does anyone make adjustments outside the books, for example your accountant at year end, in tax software or in a spreadsheet?
Who may see the output? It names logins and entries.
Must someone approve a hand-typed entry? If yes, can you export who approved each one?
Through which date are the books closed, and when was the close done?
Which accounts are sensitive, and do you know of any risk areas?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. 1 July to 30 September. The owner approves hand-typed entries over $10,000 by email, but we keep no export. Materiality is $25,000. Our outside accountant keeps year-end adjustments in a consolidation workbook. Output for the CFO and the audit committee. Books closed through 30 September, close done 9 October. Revenue, deferred revenue, the warranty reserve and equity are sensitive.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
rows: Transaction date, create date, login, description
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I review **every journal entry** that **Northbrook Trading** posted from **1 July to 30 September**, against a baseline from **the six prior quarters**. The approval limit is **$10,000** and materiality is **$25,000**.
messages.after: The consolidation workbook is not connected, so the adjustments in it are **not in this population**. You keep no approval log, so I report the four approval tests as not run. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read the population in one batch
messages.summary: 9 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: I read **1,284** transactions of all types. A person typed **48** of them by hand, which is 3.7%. Before I screen them, I prove that I read them all:

card.title: Tie-out
rows: Debits of the 1,284 transactions I read
= General ledger movement for the quarter

messages.after: The difference is 0.00, so the screen is complete. The adjustments in the consolidation workbook are not in it, and the report header says so.

messages.text: I start with the pattern, because it matters more than any one entry. In three quarters in a row, the **owner** login released the warranty reserve by hand on a Saturday:
messages.after: Each release is just below your $10,000 limit, so none needed approval. Each one brings the quarter to exactly $50,000. In total, $29,000 left the reserve. This is a question, not a finding.

messages.text: I screened all 1,284 transactions. Seven of the 48 hand-typed entries meet at least one warning sign. Three score 6 or more, so I review them:

card.title: Flagged entries, top three
head: Entry
Score
Warning signs
rows: Dated 30 Sep, typed in 12 Oct, after the close, into a closed period
Reserve, just below the limit, unusual login, "adjustment", weekend, period end
Revenue, at or above materiality, round amount, period end

messages.after: A sign gets 3, 2 or 1 points, and the report states each weight. The other four flags score 2 or less. JE-202609-022 is a routine round accrual. JE-202609-024 already corrects JE-202608-014.

messages.text: I cannot answer these three from the books. A person must give the support and the reason. I ask roles, not people. Can the bookkeeper explain JE-202609-027 and JE-202609-023?
The bookkeeper says 027 is the late September utilities bill. 023 defers the Pinnacle annual contract. Receipt and contract attached.
Thank you. Here is the follow-up for each entry:

card.title: Follow-up
head: Entry
Amount
Asked of
Result
rows: Error in the date. Move it to the open period
Open. Send the warranty claims analysis
Legitimate. It defers 11 months of an annual payment

messages.after: The error is about a date, not about a person. A person moves the date of JE-202609-027. I do not change your books. If no support arrives for JE-202609-019, it goes to the audit committee chair.

messages.text: Four of the 21 tests did not run. They need an approval log, and you keep none. The report lists them. It does not leave them out.

card.title: Control observations
head: Observation
Measure
rows: Descriptions of three words or fewer

messages.after: To run the four tests next quarter, ask for an export from whoever keeps the approval emails.

messages.text: Your review has nine sheets, with the patterns first. The header gives the population, the tie-out and that the workbook adjustments are not in it.
messages.after: Do you want the sheets as an Excel file? And do you want me to save your settings for next quarter?

messages.text: Yes to both. Please save this quarter's flags too, so we can compare.

Here is **JE_Review_2026-Q3_Northbrook Trading.xlsx**. I saved the method only. These are your sensitive accounts, the $10,000 limit, the weights, the six-quarter baseline and one rule: quarter-end accruals to 2110 are routine.
messages.after: I do not save flags, scores, logins or explanations. Next quarter, I screen every entry again from the start.
